title: Fix Adam capturable zero-lr NaNs
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.15.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #186444

The capturable single-tensor Adam path folds tensor learning-rate math into the denominator because addcdiv_ only accepts a numeric value. The old formula divided the square-rooted second moment by step_size_neg before adding eps. When lr was zero and a row had zero second moment, that formed 0 / -0.0 and the parameter update wrote NaNs even though the intended update is zero.

Fix the denominator construction so the full-precision non-differentiable path adds the epsilon term before folding in the step size. For fp16 and bfloat16 state, compute the denominator and update numerator in fp32 so eps does not underflow away. For differentiable Adam, apply the tensor step size to the numerator to avoid putting a reciprocal zero-lr singularity in the autograd graph.

The fp32 non-differentiable path keeps the low-allocation denominator folding used by the existing hot path. The low-precision and differentiable paths use the numerator form because correctness there requires avoiding underflow or a differentiable divide by zero.

Fixes #126514
Generated by my agent

Benchmark Results:
Command: python /data/users/jansel/pytorch-issue-fixer/state/126514/bench_capturable_adam.py
Device: NVIDIA B200; capturable=True, foreach=False, nparams=32, numel=1024, dtype=float32, lr=1e-3; medians in ms/step.

Eager Adam: old 3.456877, stable-fold candidate 3.288858
Eager AdamW: old 3.623303, stable-fold candidate 3.483388
Compiled Adam: old 0.262946, stable-fold candidate 0.262817
Compiled AdamW: old 0.304698, stable-fold candidate 0.269545

Zero-lr correctness check from the same benchmark: old formula produced NaN rows in untouched embedding weights; stable-fold and numerator forms were finite and left zero-lr weights unchanged.

Test Plan:
- inline CUDA repro before fix: reproduced NaNs with AdamW(lr=0.0, capturable=True, foreach=False) on nn.Embedding in eager and compiled optimizer step
- inline CUDA fp16 eager/compiled AdamW sanity check after final fix for lr=0.0 and lr=1e-3, AMSGrad on/off: passed, finite weights and zero-lr weights unchanged
- python test/test_optim.py -k test_adam_capturable_forloop_no_nan
- python test/test_optim.py TestDifferentiableOptimizer.test_adam_differentiable_zero_lr_grad_is_finite
- python test/test_optim.py TestOptimRenewedCUDA.test_foreach_matches_forloop_Adam_cuda_float64 TestOptimRenewedCUDA.test_foreach_matches_forloop_AdamW_cuda_float64
- python test/test_optim.py TestDifferentiableOptimizer.test_adam_differentiable_lr TestDifferentiableOptimizer.test_adamw_differentiable_lr
- python test/test_optim.py TestDifferentiableOptimizer.test_adam_differentiable_betas TestDifferentiableOptimizer.test_adamw_differentiable_betas
- lintrunner torch/optim/adam.py test/test_optim.py test/optim/test_optim.py
- git diff --check HEAD

lintrunner -a was also run and failed only on unrelated existing C++ clang-tidy findings in torch/csrc/shim_common.cpp, torch/csrc/stable/accelerator.h, and torch/custom_class.h.
